    About Me

    My name is Mohammad Sanad AlTaher (Sanad). I’m currently in my fourth year as a PhD student at University of Nevada, Reno in electrical engineering, researching thermal management of RF devices.

    Click for:
    Résumé LinkedIn Publications

    I previously studied at Oregon State University (Corvallis, Oregon), where I worked in the Integrated Electronics research group, and focused on electromagnetics. At OSU, I completed three years and passed the qualifying exam for a PhD in electrical and computer engineering. However, I relocated to UNR to continue research with my advisor, Prof. Tom Weller and to utilize the UNR labs and facilities.

    My current research centers on developing and testing novel passive RF devices (such as antennas, transmission lines, resonators, etc.) and thermal management approaches for them. Recently, I have worked on:

    • Coplanar waveguides (CPWs) with non-intrusive temperature measurement.
    • Planar antennas and waveguide probes for high-power testing of the CPWs.
    • Active liquid cooling test-fixtures for high-power planar transmission lines.

    Before graduate studies, I obtained my bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from Jordan University of Science and Technology, where I graduated with a 3.92/4.0 CGPA, ranking 4th in a cohort of 78 students. Additionally, I specialized in Telecommunications and ranked 1st in that track, around half of the EE cohort.

    During my undergraduate studies, I gained international experience in entrepreneurship, academics, and research through the Hult Prize in Dubai (2019), an Erasmus+ exchange semester in Istanbul (2021), and a research internship in India (2022).

    I am mostly interested in electromagnetics, RF telecommunications, and applied physics. I hope to work on developing advanced technologies in those fields after finishing my PhD.
